trial_name.text: TKT024 (Phase II/III randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study)

citations.quote: Study TKT024 was the pivotal clinical study submitted in support of the approval of idursulfase, and included safety and efficacy outcomes measures that permitted substantive clinical review.

nct.text: Not stated in the reviewed documents

TKT024, titled "A Phase II/III, Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Clinical Study Evaluating the Safety and Efficacy of Weekly and Every Other Week Dosing Regimens of Iduronate-2-Sulfatase Enzyme Replacement Therapy in Patients with MPS II"

design.text: Multicenter, international, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study comparing two idursulfase dosing regimens (weekly and every-other-week) versus placebo over 52 weeks, with 32 patients randomized to each of the three treatment groups at nine sites.

citations.quote: Study TKT024 was a multi-center, international, double-blind, placebo-controlled, safety and efficacy study performed in 96 male patients with Hunter syndrome.

The sole Phase 3 study was a 96-patient randomized, double-blind comparison of two dosing regimens of Elaprase vs. placebo for 52 weeks to evaluate safety and effects of treatment on tests of physical performance.
There were 32 patients randomized to each treatment group.

population.text: Male patients with MPS II (Hunter syndrome), ages 5 to 25 years, with I2S enzyme activity less than 10% of the lower limit of normal and normal activity of one other sulfatase; patients had to be able to stand six minutes for the walk test.

citations.quote: To be eligible, patients were required to have a diagnosis of MPS II with clinical signs and symptoms, I2S enzyme activity less than 10% of the lower limit of normal, and normal activity of one other sulfatase. Patients were required to be males between the ages of 5 and 25 years, and the needed to be capable of performing the required study testing. They were required to be able to stand six minu

endpoint.text: A two-component composite score based on the sum of the ranks of the change from baseline to Week 53 in distance walked on the six-minute walk test (6MWT) and the ranks of the change in percent-predicted forced vital capacity (%FVC).

citations.quote: The primary endpoint was a composite of distance walked on a six-minute walk test (6MWT), and forced vital capacity as a percent of predicted (%FVC).

In the pivotal study TKT024, the primary efficacy outcome assessment was a two-component composite score based on the sum of the ranks of the change from baseline to Week 53 in distance walked during a 6 Minute Walk Test (6-MWT) and the ranks of the change in %-predicted FVC.

n.text: 96 patients (32 per arm: weekly, every-other-week, placebo)

citations.quote: A total of 96 patients participated at nine sites (four in the U.S., three in England, and one each in Germany and Brazil). There were 32 patients randomized to each treatment group.

result.text: The composite primary endpoint favored weekly idursulfase vs placebo (p=0.0049). The weekly group averaged a 35 meter greater adjusted mean increase in 6MWT distance vs placebo (p=0.01); the %FVC difference (4.28) was not statistically significant (p=0.0650).

citations.quote: the difference was greatest between the placebo group and the weekly treatment group (weekly idursulfase vs. placebo, p=0.0049)
the weekly idursulfase-treated group experienced a 35 meter (38 yards) greater mean increase in the distance walked in six minutes compared to placebo

indication.text: Idursulfase (ELAPRASE) is indicated for patients with Hunter syndrome (Mucopolysaccharidosis II, MPS II); it has been shown to improve walking capacity in these patients.

citations.quote: Idursulfase is indicated for patients with Hunter syndrome (Mucopolysaccharidosis II, MPS II). Idursulfase has been shown to improve walking capacity in these patients.

target_moa.text: Idursulfase is a recombinant form of the human lysosomal enzyme iduronate-2-sulfatase (I2S), which is deficient in MPS II; it provides an exogenous source of enzyme taken up into cellular lysosomes via mannose-6-phosphate receptors, where it hydrolyzes the glycosaminoglycans dermatan sulfate and heparan sulfate.

citations.quote: Elaprase is a formulation of idursulfase, a purified form of the human lysosomal enzyme iduronate-2-sulfatase (I2S) that is produced by recombinant DNA technology in a human cell line. Elaprase provides an exogenous source of I2S that is taken up into cells and transported into lysosomes where it hydrolyzes the glycosaminoglycans (GAG) dermatan sulfate and heparan sulfate.

modality.text: Enzyme (recombinant human iduronate-2-sulfatase enzyme replacement therapy)

citations.quote: Elaprase is a formulation of idursulfase, a purified form of the human lysosomal enzyme iduronate-2-sulfatase (I2S) that is produced by recombinant DNA technology in a human cell line.

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (>=10% and more frequent than placebo) included pyrexia (63% vs 59%), headache (59% vs 44%), arthralgia (31% vs 28%), and pruritus (28% vs 16%). The most serious risk was infusion reactions: 16/108 patients (15%) experienced infusion reactions during 26 of 8,274 infusions (0.3%), including life-threatening anaphylactic reactions.

Life-threatening anaphylactic reactions have been observed in some patients during ELAPRASE infusions.

detail.text: Risk of anaphylaxis: life-threatening anaphylactic reactions have been observed during ELAPRASE infusions, so appropriate medical support should be readily available. Biphasic anaphylactic reactions have occurred and may require prolonged observation; patients with compromised respiratory function or acute respiratory disease may be at risk of serious acute exacerbation and require additional monitoring.

citations.quote: Life-threatening anaphylactic reactions have been observed in some patients during ELAPRASE infusions. Therefore, appropriate medical support should be readily available when ELAPRASE is administered. Biphasic anaphylactic reactions have also been observed after ELAPRASE administration and patients who have experienced anaphylactic reactions may require prolonged observation. Patients with compromised respiratory function or acute respiratory disease may be at risk of serious acute exacerbation of their respiratory compromise due to infusion reactions, and require additional monitoring.

detail.text: The BLA was submitted November 23, 2005 and granted priority review; a request for additional information on anaphylactoid/angioedema reactions extended the review clock, and the product was approved in this review cycle (no prior CRL or refuse-to-file stated).

citations.quote: On November 23, 2005, Transkaryotic Therapies, Inc, submitted BLA STN 125151 which was granted a priority review. A request in May 2006 for additional information regarding the occurrence of anaphylactoid and angioedema reactions after idursulfase infusion prompted an extension of the review clock.
Submission date: November 23, 2005

requirement.text: Evaluate long-term safety and efficacy data in an observational survey (Hunter Outcome Survey, HOS) of patients with Hunter syndrome treated with ELAPRASE, collecting data including the six-minute walk test and urinary GAG levels approximately every 6 to 12 months for at least 15 years.

citations.quote: Shire commits to evaluating long-term safety and efficacy data in an observational survey (the Hunter Outcome Survey, HOS) of patients with Hunter syndrome being treated with ELAPRASE.

the survey will collect data from patients on the six-minute walk test, from a subset of centers that will have the training and facilities to collect the data in a standardized and reproducible manner, and urinary GAG levels approximately every 6 to 12 months for at least 15 years.

requirement.text: Conduct a study to evaluate pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, and safety in at least 18 children 5 years of age and under treated with ELAPRASE for at least 6 months.

citations.quote: Shire commits to conducting a study to evaluate pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, and safety in at least 18 children 5 years of age and under treated with ELAPRASE for at least 6 months.
